source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New Jersey has 48 mapped data centers but only five publish power capacity, and CyrusOne's NYM2 in Totowa discloses 6 MW of IT load.

That gap is the pattern. The state's mapped footprint is roughly ten times the number of facilities that publish a power figure, and NYM2's 6 MW is 5.4 percent of the 111.3 MW disclosed statewide, ranking fourth among the five. What can be measured about New Jersey data center capacity is a small subset of what has been built.

Six megawatts is a modest figure for AI. At the 40 kW per rack typical of AI training density, it translates to roughly 150 racks, and the operator's specification does not break that down by workload or accelerator type. Set against 200,000 square feet of technical space, the published numbers describe a building with far more floor area than its disclosed power would densely fill. SSAE 16 Type II certification speaks to security and availability controls, not to compute scale. The suitability score of 52 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion absent.

What the data does not cover matters here. There is no power distribution architecture, no cooling capacity, and no grid connection detail. So it cannot be determined whether 6 MW is a limit set by the grid, by internal thermal design, or by the operator's own disclosure choices. Whether this campus matters for AI scaling depends on grid headroom in northern New Jersey and on capacity CyrusOne has not published.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
